<p class="cycle-role">The arrangements through which climate action becomes operable.</p>

<p class="page-deck"><strong>Through which institutional arrangements does urban climate action become possible and durable?</strong></p>

Evidence and ambition do not implement themselves. Urban climate action becomes possible through particular configurations of authority, finance, organisational capability, infrastructure provision, participation, coordination, sequencing and maintenance. Similar interventions may therefore follow very different delivery routes across cities.

This theme compares how these configurations are assembled across city types, sectors and institutional settings. We examine which mechanisms make action operable, how responsibilities and resources are combined over time, why delivery arrangements endure or fail, and how they change as political, fiscal and social conditions shift. The aim is not to identify one universal delivery model, but to distinguish recurring patterns from context-dependent arrangements.

::: {.notice}
**Analytical boundary.** A delivery mode is a configuration through which change becomes operable. It is not merely a technology, sector, policy instrument or list of actors.

**Place in the learning cycle.** Delivery arrangements shape which consequences occur, who experiences them and whether climate action can be maintained over time.
:::

## Questions the lab investigates

- How are urban climate actions authorised, financed, coordinated and maintained?
- Which configurations of authority, capability and participation make delivery possible?
- How do sequencing, contestation and institutional learning affect durability?

<div class="idea-grid"><article class="idea-card"><p class="idea-disclaimer">Research idea · not currently an active or funded project</p><h3>Which configurations of authority, finance, capability and participation recur across different city types?</h3><p>Comparing configurations may reveal recurring mechanisms while preserving the institutional conditions that make them work differently across places.</p><h4>Suggested methods</h4><ul class="method-list"><li>comparative case studies</li><li>qualitative comparative analysis</li><li>institutional mapping</li><li>process tracing</li><li>configurational analysis</li></ul></article><article class="idea-card"><p class="idea-disclaimer">Research idea · not currently an active or funded project</p><h3>How do delivery arrangements change between policy adoption, implementation and long-term maintenance?</h3><p>Following arrangements over time could identify where authority, resources and accountability shift after policy adoption.</p><h4>Suggested methods</h4><ul class="method-list"><li>longitudinal process tracing</li><li>event sequence analysis</li><li>policy document archives</li><li>organisational interviews</li><li>implementation history comparison</li></ul></article><article class="idea-card"><p class="idea-disclaimer">Research idea · not currently an active or funded project</p><h3>How do federal and provincial institutions enable or constrain municipal climate delivery in Canada?</h3><p>Municipal action depends on intergovernmental authority and finance, but these relationships may vary across provinces, sectors and city types.</p><h4>Suggested methods</h4><ul class="method-list"><li>multilevel governance comparison</li><li>intergovernmental fiscal analysis</li><li>paired municipal cases</li><li>policy network analysis</li><li>comparative institutional analysis</li></ul></article></div>

## Connections across the learning cycle

- **Input from [Where New Evidence Matters](/research/where-new-evidence-matters.html):** New evidence matters most when it changes what decision-makers understand about how climate action can be delivered or what it may cause.
- **Next stage — [Consequences for People and Places](/research/consequences-for-people-and-places.html):** Delivery arrangements shape which consequences occur, who experiences them and whether climate action can be maintained over time.
- **Return loop:** Consequences generate new evidence, reveal unresolved questions and revise what other cities may plausibly learn.
